[NDLC.3.1] The construct capabilities that gate a surface construct, and
when a tier sets each `false`:

| Capability | Language surface | Set `false` when |
|---|---|---|
| `call` | `call <domain>.<method> ...` | tier has no adapter or service connection, or can't absorb call latency |
| `publish` | `publish <Schema> ...` | tier is the topmost (has nowhere to publish to) |
| `cache` | `cache key: k value: v` | rules on this tier must not mutate cache state |
| `cache_delete` | `cache_delete key: k` | rules on this tier must not mutate cache state |
| `nocooldown` | the bare `nocooldown` flag on `call` ([LCRS.8.1]) | tier requires an explicit rate bound on every call |
| `series` | `series ...` declaration plus the aggregation surface ([LFCA.5.1]) | tier has no series subsystem — no backend is registered for the series atoms the artefact would carry |

The capabilities with engine consequences (`realtime`, `constspace`,
`linear_scan`, `logical`, `dynamic_ttl`, `regex`, `float`) are specified in
[LCAP.2]. The storage and samples-plane capabilities are deferred, and every
dialect sets them `false` ([LCAP.2.10]).

`cached(...)` is **not** a capability and is not gateable. The cache is
engine-owned — every engine has one, a read takes no integrator callback,
so there is no tier that lacks it ([LFCA.2.4]); only the two cache write
verbs above are gateable.
